title: Encapsulating Cytochrome c in Silica Aerogel Nanoarchitectures without Metal Nanoparticles while Retaining Gas-phase Bioactivity
protocol: Wear safety glasses or goggles at all times during the procedure.
Wear a laboratory coat at all times during the procedure.
Wear laboratory gloves at all times during the procedure.
Operate the critical point drying apparatus only with safety glasses or goggles.
Process solutions containing tetramethoxysilane, methanol, ethanol, acetone, and ammonia within a fume hood.
Weigh out 2.72 g of potassium phosphate monobasic and dissolve in water using a 500 ml volumetric flask to prepare 500 ml of 0.04 M potassium phosphate monobasic solution.
Weigh out 3.48 g of potassium phosphate dibasic and dissolve in water using a 500 ml volumetric flask to prepare 500 ml of 0.04 M potassium phosphate dibasic solution.
Pour the dibasic salt solution into a large beaker with a stir bar and begin stirring.
Slowly add portions of the monobasic salt solution to the dibasic salt solution while monitoring the pH until it reaches 7.00.
Weigh out approximately 0.023 g of cyt. c and place in glass scintillation vial.
Add 2,000 μl of prepared potassium phosphate buffer using a micropipette to the cyt. c.
Gently swirl the solution until all solid cyt. c has dissolved into the solution and no particulate matter remains.
Take 20 μl of the prepared cyt. c solution and add to a 1-cm path length plastic cuvette.
Add 3 ml of prepared buffer to the cuvette.
Take UV-vis spectrum from 300-700 nm using buffer in the reference cell.
Determine the concentration of the cyt. c solution at 409 nm using the Beer-Lambert law.
Back calculate the concentration of the original prepared cyt. c solution.
Pipette 117 μl of 0.72 mM prepared cyt. c solution into a scintillation vial.
Add 683 μl of prepared buffer to the vial containing 117 μl of cyt. c solution.
Swirl to mix thoroughly.
Store original prepared and diluted cyt. c solutions at 2-8°C in a refrigerator until ready to use for up to two weeks.
Label a disposable 50 ml polypropylene beaker 'Beaker A'.
Add 1.88 g tetramethoxysilane into the labeled beaker using a glass Pasteur pipette.
Cover 'Beaker A' with Parafilm after zeroing the balance and adding methanol.
Label a disposable 50 ml polypropylene beaker 'Beaker B'.
Add a magnetic stir bar to Beaker B and place it on an analytical balance.
Use a glass pipette to add 0.75 g water to Beaker B.
Add 3.00 g methanol to Beaker B.
Cover Beaker B with Parafilm.
Begin stirring the contents of Beaker B on a stir plate inside a fume hood.
Insert 5 μl of 28.0-30.0% ammonium hydroxide solution through the Parafilm cover into the mixture while stirring.
Add the contents of 'Beaker A' to Beaker B as soon as step is complete.
Stir the mixture for 20 min while covered in Parafilm.
Acquire 8-9 polypropylene scintillation vials and corresponding caps.
Put plastic wrap over the cap end of each vial to create a flat surface for the gel to form on.
Place the cap over each vial making sure that the plastic wrap stays intact inside the cap.
Line up the vials with cap-end down on the bench top and opened bottoms facing up.
Add 3 ml of the sol mixture to a clean disposable 50 ml polypropylene beaker.
Use a glass Pasteur pipette to slowly drop 500 μl of the 0.105 mM diluted cyt. c solution to the 3 ml sol mixture over ~1 min.
Gently swirl the mixture while adding the cyt. c to avoid formation of large red clumps.
Pipet 0.5 ml of the resulting cyt. c silica sol into each prepared mold.
Pipet 0.5 ml of remaining 'plain' silica sol into one or two molds as control samples during supercritical drying process.
Cover the face-up openings of the molds with Parafilm and put in refrigerator (~2-8 °C) overnight or for at least 12 hr to produce sol-gels.
Remove the Parafilm from the top of one mold containing a cyt. c sol-gel.
Remove the cap and plastic wrap from the bottom of the mold.
Add some ethanol into the mold using a wash bottle.
Use the circular disk end of a syringe plunger to carefully push the gel out of the mold.
Place the gel into a clean 20 ml glass scintillation vial containing approximately 5 ml of ethanol.
Repeat this gel removal procedure until all cyt. c gels are added to one vial and all silica gels are added to another vial.
Store like gels together within separate vials.
Fill the vials to the top with ethanol.
Cap and store the vials between 2-8 °C.
Every four hours, remove the gels from the refrigerator.
Decant the ethanol off the gels.
Replace with fresh ethanol.
Submerge the wet sol gels in acetone.
Decant and add fresh acetone three times a day for three days.
Cool a critical point drying apparatus to 10 °C by setting the circulator temperature to 8 °C.
Once the apparatus reaches 10 °C, perform a leak test by adding acetone inside.
Open the fill valve of the apparatus.
Add carbon dioxide until the apparatus is half-full.
Close the fill valve and check for hissing at doors and valves.
Replace any O-rings or seals if a leak is found.
After completing the leak test, open the drain valve to release acetone and carbon dioxide into the fume hood drain.
Ensure the apparatus is leak-free.
Carefully pour wet gels and most of the acetone from scintillation vials into the transfer boat's three long sections.
Push and move gels within the boat with forceps to ensure complete submersion in acetone.
Add more acetone if needed before sealing the boat inside the apparatus.
Open the fill valve of the apparatus to add carbon dioxide.
Open the drain valve for five minutes as soon as acetone starts sinking to the bottom through the window.
Close the drain valve after five minutes.
Keep the fill valve cracked open slightly.
Repeat opening the drain valve for five minutes and adjusting the fill valve to keep the apparatus full during draining.
Close the drain valve again after each five-minute period.
Open the drain for 5 min at a time approximately every 40 min over at least six hours.
Adjust the fill valve during draining to ensure the liquid level in the apparatus never drops below the top of the boat.
Close the fill valve once draining steps are complete.
Drain liquid carbon dioxide so that its level remains visible just above the prongs on the boat through the apparatus window.
Set the temperature of the attached circulator to 40 °C.
Observe the transition from liquid to supercritical fluid through the apparatus window as the liquid meniscus disappears.
Allow at least 15 min of equilibration time after observing the transition.
Open the vent valve a small amount to begin releasing the supercritical fluid.
Over the course of approximately 45 min, incrementally open the vent valve wider so that a steady but low hiss is heard and pressure gauge slowly decreases to zero.
After apparatus pressure goes to zero, open apparatus door.
Remove boat from apparatus using forceps.
Place newly dried aerogels in clean glass scintillation vials.
Cut out 2.5 cm x 2.5 cm piece of lightweight cardboard, fold it in half, cut halfway up on the fold, then fold flaps back.
Cut out 5 cm x 5 cm piece of lightweight cardboard with a 1.5 cm x 1.5 cm square hole in the middle.
Use black electrical tape to decrease size of hold to 0.5 cm x 0.5 cm.
Tape flaps of folded and cut cardboard against 5 cm x 5 cm piece of cardboard to create small bent surface for aerogel monoliths.
Tape back piece of cardboard to UV-visible spectrophotometer so hole is in line with beam path.
Measure thickness of gels with micrometer.
Place one gel on the cardboard platform.
Measure a spectrum from 300-800 nm with air in the reference compartment of the UV-visible spectrophotometer.
Fit a polynomial, A = aλ^n, to the wavelength region where the absorbance is mainly due to background scattering (~700-800 nm).
Calculate the scatter at other wavelengths using the coefficients obtained from the fit.
Subtract calculated scatter background absorbance from the raw spectrum to obtain a scatter corrected spectrum.
Fit the scatter subtracted spectrum with a Gaussian curve in the region of 370 to 490 nm using appropriate software (GRAMS/AI 8.0).
Determine the peak height, peak center, and peak width of the Soret peak of the aerogel.
Apply the Beer-Lambert Law using the measured thickness of the gel for path length (l), the extinction coefficient (ε) of 106,100 M-1cm-1, and the Soret peak height (A).
Compute the concentration (c) of cyt. c in the aerogel using A = εlc.
Compare the calculated cyt. c concentration to the theoretical 15 μM concentration in the gel.
Run nitrogen in the CD instrument for at least 5 minutes before turning on the lamp.
Tape the cardboard holder to the CD spectrometer so the hole aligns with the beam path.
Measure a continuous wavelength blank spectrum from 350-500 nm at 100 nm/min, averaging three scans with nothing in the holder.
Place one gel on the cardboard platform and measure its spectrum from 350-500 nm at 100 nm/min, averaging three scans.
Repeat UV-visible and CD measurements for all aerogel monoliths of interest.
Detect presence of NO gas using cyt. c-silica aerogels in a fume hood.
Handle all NO gas safely to prevent exposure to air, which can form nitrogen dioxide or nitrogen tetroxide.
Avoid contact between NO and water to prevent the production of heat and corrosive fumes.
Place an 8 L nitric oxide cylinder in a well-ventilated fume hood and adjust the pressure to 4 psi.
Connect tubing to both the nitric oxide cylinder and a nitrogen cylinder (pressure set to 6 psi).
Link up the ends of the tubing to a T-valve.
Measure the thickness of the aerogel monolith with a micrometer.
Place the aerogel (~3 mm thick) in a disposable cuvette with plastic cap.
Put the cuvette into the spectrophotometer and cut the aerogel slightly if necessary to fit in the cuvette.
Insert two syringe needles into the plastic cap of the cuvette, one connected to the output of the T-valve and one as exhaust into the fume hood.
Seal the needles to the tubing with Parafilm and seal the cap to the cuvette with Parafilm.
Place an empty disposable cuvette in the reference cell.
Adjust the aerogel cuvette position to ensure that the aerogel lies in the beam path prior to starting the experiment.
Take an initial spectrum from 800 to 300 nm.
Monitor the difference between the absorbance at 414 nm and the absorbance at 408 nm while turning the T-valve to switch between nitrogen and the nitric oxide/nitrogen mixture at set time intervals.
Ensure that the flow rate of nitrogen or nitric oxide/nitrogen mixture is not so high that the aerogel moves around in the cuvette.
Take a final spectrum from 800 to 300 nm once the exposure cycles are finished.
Repeat the procedure with three to four monoliths to obtain an average sensing response.
